Foundation and production evidence
Establish a repeatable baseline and decide what can be safely reused.
Measure the existing levels
Measure smooth runs and observed first attempts, including time, deaths, secrets and reuse decisions; record build and participants.
Audit asset provenance and redistribution
Inventory code, art, music, fonts and effects with sources, licenses, permitted uses and unresolved items; identify replacement or clearance actions.
Establish reproducible import and test baseline
Document and run clean Godot import and representative integration tests; investigate import metadata consistency and record limitations.
Define the playtest and device plan
Define participant groups, consent, measures, test builds, target devices and quantitative thresholds before formal testing.
Solo controls, recovery and assists
Make the solo experience readable, fair, and faithful to the GDD.
Calibrate movement and contextual interaction
Verify jump assists, movement and interaction prompts; resolve accidental action conflicts and record playtest observations.
Implement attempt recovery and depletion rules
Verify falls, safe points, health depletion and attempt inventory reset while retaining previously recorded progress; cover edge cases in tests.
Add configurable accessibility assists
Provide extra hearts, checkpoint frequency and no fall damage with no content penalty; test normal and assisted recovery.
Campaign progression and persistence
Support durable progress, level selection and replay.
Design and implement versioned campaign saves
Define durable versus attempt state; save and reload progress safely with versioning and corruption handling; test restart and migration paths.
Create campaign registry and level map
Define level metadata, sequential unlocks and revisiting; display open and completed routes and test transition behavior.
Persist secrets, rewards and character unlocks
Record secrets and discoveries, world rewards and the campaign-completion prototype unlock; verify reload and replay behavior.
Local cooperative play
Make the complete main route playable by one or two people.
Implement player input and character assignment
Support distinct device ownership, safe join and leave, equal abilities and no player collision; exercise keyboard plus controller and two controllers.
Implement shared camera and safe relocation
Keep both players readable; cue and safely relocate a distant player without penalty, including obstructed terrain cases.
Implement cooperative health, revival and shared exits
Implement separate hearts, partner respawn, both-out restart, shared key and exit rules; test deadlocks, falls and join/leave transitions.
Representative playable slice
Build a four-level world that tests the core experience before scaling.
Design and validate protagonist presentation
Develop Lila and Sol reference sheets and readable in-game silhouettes and animations; test at game size and in grayscale.
Build four distinct slice levels and finale
Create introduction, combination, exploration and finale levels with readable routes, one optional secret each and a restored light; test solo and co-op.
Prototype a discovery path and album
Build one optional post-ending path with category, reward and persistent album record; make it replayable solo and co-op.
Add slice narrative and audiovisual feedback
Implement a skippable visual introduction, clear interaction and hazard cues and celebration; validate readability without relying on text or audio alone.
Playtest and scope decision
Gather evidence and decide the feasible campaign scope.
Observe slice playtests and record findings
Observe players including ages 5–7 with appropriate adult consent and varied experience; record comprehension, retries, assistance, enjoyment and times.
Decide campaign scope from slice evidence
Review test results, resource constraints and risks; document the decision on level count, co-op, discovery paths and next milestones without assuming approval.
Campaign production
Complete the approved campaign and its ending after the slice gate.
Plan and produce worlds 2–4
After the scope decision, prepare level briefs and build approved world content, finales and secrets; verify every mandatory route solo and co-op.
Plan and produce worlds 5–6
After the scope decision, prototype wind and creature behaviors safely and produce approved levels and finales with readable cues.
Plan and produce worlds 7–8 and ending
Produce approved late-game combinations, final Wind encounter and visual ending; verify progression and accessibility without secrets.
Replayability and discovery
Deliver rewarding optional exploration without blocking the ending.
Implement exploration and reward presentation
Expose completed level selection, secret log, illustrations and prototype character after their defined unlocks; persist and test them.
Expand discovery paths based on prototype results
Decide quantity after evaluation; author approved paths with distinct categories, source real facts, label fiction and verify development stories.
Evaluate optional mastery challenges
Prototype and evaluate optional challenges including the proposed world restart rule; document decision and keep the standard campaign unaffected.
Quality, accessibility and release
Validate a distributable game on selected platforms.
Implement Spanish-first localization and accessible interface
Prepare translation-ready text, Spanish initial UI, visual prompts and accessible options; test readability, remapping and no color-only information.
Validate desktop and browser builds
Define supported versions and test real Linux, macOS, Windows and browser builds for input, saving, audio, performance and web hosting.
Complete release audit and regression pass
Resolve distribution rights, run automated and human regressions, document known issues and release criteria; verify no unresolved blocking rights.
Optional playtest telemetry
Provide voluntary, privacy-conscious evidence for balancing if approved.
Define telemetry policy and event schema
Specify consent, retention, ownership, event versions, denominators and local identifiers before real collection; prohibit automatic transmission.
Implement opt-in local collection and controls
Default off; provide local review, deletion and export; exclude pauses, avoid personal data and test with synthetic sessions on desktop and web.
Analyze synthetic telemetry and validate interpretation
Validate heatmap cells, attempt denominators and performance; document limits of interpreting exits and retention before collecting real sessions.
